entities.label: AISystem
entities.rationale: An AI system is a material entity: it has physical instantiation (hardware, substrate) and spatial extent. It is a kind (common noun), so modeled as a class.

entities.label: JuridicalRole

The existing working:LegalRight and working:CourtAuthority are already typed as BFO_0000023, but 'JuridicalRole' is a more general class for any legally conferred role that an entity may bear.

relations.rationale: AISystem is a subclass of Material entity (BFO_0000040).
JuridicalRole is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023), as it is an externally grounded socio-legal function.

The thesis requires that JuridicalRole inheres in (RO_0000052) some AISystem. This is expressed as an OWL existential restriction: JuridicalRole subClassOf (RO_0000052 some AISystem). This encodes the claim that an AI system CAN be a bearer of a juridical role — i.e., there exist instances of JuridicalRole that inhere in AISystem instances.

Should working:JuridicalRole be typed as a subclass of an existing working class such as working:LegalRight or working:CourtAuthority, or should it remain a direct subclass of BFO_0000023 as a more general category?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two ontological commitments: (1) digital personhood is a legal status — typed as a Role (BFO_0000023) because legal statuses are externally conferred, socially grounded properties that inhere in bearers; and (2) this status is realized in institutional recognition — which requires a Process (BFO_0000015) as the realization target per BFO's realized-in relation (BFO_0000054). proposal.utterance: A smart contract encodes obligations as executable patterns.

entities.label: SmartContract
entities.rationale: A smart contract is an information artifact — an encoded pattern of rules and obligations that can be concretized in multiple substrates (blockchain nodes, VMs). It is a generically dependent continuant because its content (the encoded logic) is what matters, and it can in principle be copied or migrated. It is a class because 'smart contract' is a common noun denoting a kind.

entities.label: ExecutableObligation
entities.rationale: An obligation encoded in a smart contract is still a role (externally grounded normative function) borne by a party, but distinguished by being operationalized as a machine-executable pattern. Typing as a subclass of the existing LegalObligation (which is BFO_0000023/Role) is appropriate. The 'executable' qualifier is a specific mode of concretization.

entities.label: ExecutablePattern
entities.rationale: An executable pattern is a generically dependent continuant — a piece of information (algorithm, bytecode logic) that can be concretized in and copied across computational substrates. The utterance identifies this as what a smart contract encodes, distinct from the obligation itself which is a role.

relations.rationale: SmartContract is a kind of generically dependent continuant — an information artifact.
ExecutableObligation is a specialization of LegalObligation, distinguished by being encoded as an executable pattern.
ExecutablePattern is a kind of generically dependent continuant — an algorithmic/informational structure.
A smart contract has as part the executable pattern that encodes the obligations — the content of the smart contract includes the executable logic.

The executable obligation (a realizable role) is realized in the execution of the executable pattern — the process of running the smart contract logic realizes the encoded obligation. Note: BFO_0000054 (realized in) is a relation from realizable to process; here ExecutablePattern is treated as the process-type context in which the obligation is realized. Open question flagged below about whether ExecutablePattern should be a process type instead.

open_questions: Should 'ExecutablePattern' be typed as a Process (BFO_0000015) representing the execution event, or remain a generically dependent continuant representing the encoded algorithm? The utterance says obligations are encoded 'as' executable patterns, suggesting the pattern is the informational artifact, not the execution event itself — but BFO_0000054 (realized in) requires a process as the range.
Is 'SmartContract' intended to be a subclass of an existing working class such as 'Statute' or 'LegalForm', given that smart contracts may function as legally binding instruments?

Should 'ExecutableObligation' be restricted to obligations arising in smart contracts specifically, or is it a broader class covering any computationally encoded obligation (e.g., regulatory compliance rules in code)?
Is the encoding relation between SmartContract and ExecutableObligation best modeled as BFO_0000051 (has part), or would a custom 'encodes' object property be more precise here?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that smart contracts encode obligations as executable patterns, introducing three new ontological kinds. A SmartContract is a generically dependent continuant (information artifact) that has as part an ExecutablePattern (also a GDC — the algorithmic logic). ExecutableObligation is a role subclassing the existing LegalObligation, distinguishing obligations that are concretized as machine-executable code. The BFO_0000054 (realized in) relation is used to link ExecutableObligation to ExecutablePattern, though this raises a typing tension because BFO_0000054 expects a process in its range — this is flagged as an open question. The analysis conservatively reuses the existing LegalObligation class and BFO GDC typing, avoiding inflation of new classes beyond what the utterance strictly commits to.

entities.label: AutonomousAgent
entities.rationale: An autonomous agent is a material entity capable of acting in processes. Typed as Material entity (BFO_0000040) because agents have physical substrate (computational or biological) with mass and spatial extent. If purely abstract agents are intended, this could shift to a role; flagged in open_questions.

entities.label: ProcessOfRecognition
entities.rationale: Recognition is already modeled as SocialRecognition (Process) in the ontology. ProcessOfRecognition is proposed as a broader class (or we could reuse SocialRecognition). However, the utterance may intend a non-social, non-conscious form of recognition distinct from SocialRecognition. Flagged in open_questions; provisionally a new subclass of BFO_0000015.

entities.label: NonConsciousRecognition
entities.rationale: The absence-of-consciousness aspect of the agent's recognition participation is a quality inhering in the ProcessOfRecognition or the AutonomousAgent. Modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) capturing the non-conscious character of the recognition process. Flagged in open_questions as this could alternatively be a Disposition.

relations.rationale: ProcessOfRecognition is a subtype of SocialRecognition (which is already typed as BFO_0000015 Process) to capture the broader category that includes non-conscious recognition events, while SocialRecognition implies more typical intersubjective recognition.
BFO relation participates_in (RO_0000056) links AutonomousAgent (continuant) to ProcessOfRecognition (process), per the utterance's claim that the agent participates in recognition processes.

NonConsciousRecognition (Quality) inheres in ProcessOfRecognition, capturing that these recognition processes lack consciousness as a quality of those processes. Alternatively this quality could inhere in the AutonomousAgent; flagged in open_questions.

open_questions: Is 'autonomous agent' intended as a material entity (e.g., a software agent running on hardware) or as an abstract/functional role that could be borne by either a material or immaterial entity? If the latter, AutonomousAgent should be typed as Role (BFO_0000023) rather than Material entity.

Should ProcessOfRecognition be a subclass of existing SocialRecognition, or is it a distinct parallel class? The utterance implies recognition without social/conscious underpinning, which may conflict with SocialRecognition's connotation.

Is 'without consciousness' best modeled as a Quality inhering in the agent, a Quality inhering in the process, or a negative Disposition (lack of consciousness disposition) borne by the agent? The current proposal places it as a Quality of the process.
Does 'autonomous agent' refer to a specific individual (e.g., a particular AI system) or a general kind? If the former, an individual should be minted.
Is this utterance making an ontological claim about all autonomous agents (a universal), or about a specific class of agents in the legal/institutional context being modeled?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance introduces three ontological commitments: (1) a kind of entity, the AutonomousAgent, capable of participating in processes; (2) a kind of process, ProcessOfRecognition, in which the agent participates; and (3) a quality of non-consciousness that characterizes how that participation occurs. AutonomousAgent is provisionally typed as Material entity (BFO_0000040) since agents typically have physical substrate, but this is flagged as uncertain. ProcessOfRecognition is typed as a Process (BFO_0000015) and placed as a subclass of existing SocialRecognition to maintain continuity with the working ontology, though the non-conscious character may warrant a parallel rather than sub-class relation. NonConsciousRecognition is typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in the process. The key relations used are participates_in (RO_0000056) and inheres_in (RO_0000052). Several open questions concern the precise typing of the agent and whether the absence-of-consciousness is best modeled as quality, negative disposition, or a constraint on the process class itself.
